questions.question: Who received the in-principle approval from the RBI to operate as a cross-border payment aggregator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both PayPal and Worldline.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **PayPal and Worldline received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to operate as cross-border payment aggregators.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **RBI Approval:** Both PayPal and Worldline received RBI approval to facilitate cross-border online transactions.
 
• **Cross-border Payments:** This enables the companies to handle imports and exports of goods and services in India.
 
• **Regulatory Change:** RBI mandated separate approval for cross-border payment aggregators after October 2024.
 
• **Business Opportunity:** The move is crucial for tapping into India's large remittance and freelance service sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Payment Aggregator License:** Previously, cross-border payment companies operated with an Online Payment Gateway Service Provider (OPGSP) license.
 
• **Impact:** The RBI approval boosts the global payment network for businesses in India, including large enterprises and freelancers.
 
• **Freelance Sector:** India is a hub for freelancers, making the cross-border payment space highly lucrative.
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, governs the approval process for payment aggregators.

questions.question: What is the new transaction limit for UPI 123Pay after the RBI increase?

questions.question: What is the newly declared age for minors to operate bank accounts independently, as per the Reserve Bank of India’s recent guidelines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed minors above the age of 10 years to independently operate savings/term deposit accounts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Minors aged 10 years and above can now open and operate savings or term deposit accounts independently, according to RBI's new guidelines.
 
• Banks are required to ensure that minor accounts are not overdrawn and always maintain a credit balance.
 
• Additional facilities like internet banking, debit cards, and cheque books may be offered based on the bank’s risk management policy.
 
• The new guidelines will be effective by July 1, 2025, and banks must amend their policies to align with the updated rules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India**__

 
 
• Headquarters: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India
 
• **Established: 1 April 1935**
 
• **​Governor: Sanjay Malhotra**
 
 
 
• **Key People:**
 
 
• Sanjay Malhotra (Governor)
 
• M. Rajeshwar Rao (Deputy Governor)
 
• Swaminathan Janakiraman (Deputy Governor)
 
• T. Rabi Sankar (Deputy Governor)
 
• Poonam Gupta (Economist, Deputy Governor)
 
 
 
• **​Agency Overview:**
 
 
• Jurisdiction: Government of India
 
• Child Agency: Monetary Policy Committee
 
• Key Document: **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**
 
 
 
• **Functions:**
 
 
• Responsible for regulating the Indian banking system and currency
 
• Manages the supply and issuance of the Indian Rupee
 
• Promotes economic development
 
• Works on regulating payment systems through National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
 
• Prints and mints Indian currency notes through Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran (BRBNM) division
 
• Provides deposit insurance and credit guarantees through the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
 
 
 
• **Historical Facts:**
 
 
• Commenced operations on 1 April 1935, as per the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
 
• Nationalized on 1 January 1949, post India’s independence
 
 
 
• **Leadership Structure: **Direction of RBI is managed by a 21-member central board of directors, including:
 
 
• Governor
 
• Four Deputy Governors
 
• Two representatives from the Ministry of Finance
 
• Ten government-nominated directors
 
• Four directors from local boards in Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, and Delhi, each with five members representing regional interests

questions.question: What new feature has the RBI introduced for international transactions to enhance security?

options.text: One-Time Password (OTP) for all online transactions
Biometric Authentication for domestic transactions only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced the Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA) for international transactions to enhance security.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **RBI's new move introduces AFA for cross-border "Card Not Present" (CNP) transactions.**
 
• AFA will bring international transactions made with Indian-issued cards under the same security standards applied to domestic transactions.
 
• The AFA will ensure that international transactions are secured with OTP or biometric authentication, reducing the risk of fraud.
 
• This decision comes as online shopping and international digital payments have surged in India, leading to increased fraud risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• AFA for CNP Transactions__

 __
 
• Involves the use of OTP or biometric authentication to verify transactions.
 
• Aims to align international transactions with the security measures used for domestic payments.
 
 
 
• Card Not Present (CNP) Transactions__
 __
 
• Transactions where a physical card is not used, typically occurring online.
 
• Includes online purchases from international retailers.
 
 
 
• RBI's Role__
 
 
• RBI aims to enhance digital payment security to prevent fraud in the growing online transaction sector.
 
• RBI's move aligns with India's broader efforts to ensure safer and more secure digital financial systems.

questions.question: RBI Financial Stability Report, June 2025. How often is the Financial Stability Report (FSR) released by the RBI?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is ​__**Biannually**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• RBI Financial Stability Report, June 2025.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
The **Financial Stability Report (FSR)** is a **biannual report** released by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.

 
 
• 
 
It reflects the collective view of the **FSDC Sub-Committee** on the **resilience of India’s financial system** and **risks to stability**.

 
 
• 
 
**India’s GDP** grew by **6.5% in 2024–25**, the **highest among major economies**.

 
 
• 
 
**Inflation** dropped to **2.82% in May 2025**, the **lowest since February 2019**.

 
 
• 
 
**Total exports** hit a record **USD 824.9 billion in 2024–25**.

 
 
• 
 
India continues to be a **key driver of global growth**, supported by **strong macro fundamentals** and **prudent policies**.

 
 
• 
 
Risks to growth include **geopolitical tensions**, **trade disruptions**, and **weather-related uncertainties**.

 
 
• 
 
**Gross NPAs (GNPAs)** stood at **2.3% (March 2025)** and could **rise to 2.5%** in the **baseline scenario**.

 
 
• 
 
For **46 banks** (covering **98% of SCB assets**), GNPAs may increase to **2.6% by March 2027**.

 
 
• 
 
**Capital adequacy** remains **well above regulatory requirements**, even under **severe stress scenarios**.

 
 
• 
 
The **banking sector** shows **strong resilience** with **healthy buffers**.

 
 
• 
 
**NBFCs** are in **good health**, showing **robust earnings**, **strong capital**, and **improving asset quality**.

 
 
• 
 
India’s growth is **domestically driven**, with **favorable food inflation** due to **record crop production**.

 
 
• 
 
The **financial system** (banks + NBFCs) is **stable**, with **healthy balance sheets**.

questions.question: What initiative did the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) launch, to test innovative products for its Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Retail Sandbox.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) launched a retail sandbox for its Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) on October 8, 2025, to encourage fintech innovation for the e-Rupee retail pilot.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The sandbox initiative allows fintech companies to test and deploy new digital payment solutions within a controlled environment.**
 
• **Launched on December 1, 2022, the e-Rupee retail pilot will now be expanded with the sandbox framework to foster innovation and development.**
 
• **India’s e-Rupee, unlike cryptocurrencies, is a regulated digital currency issued by the RBI and holds the same value as physical currency.**
 
• **This move reinforces India's efforts to become a leader in the adoption of digital currencies globally.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)__

 __
 
• A government-issued digital currency, representing a digital form of national currency, unlike decentralized cryptocurrencies.
 
 
 
• Sandbox Environment__
 __
 
• A secure environment where new technologies, such as digital currencies, can be tested without impacting the broader financial system.
 
 
 
• e-Rupee__
 
 
• India’s official digital currency, issued by RBI, designed to complement the physical currency and serve as a legal tender in digital form.

questions.question: What is the new facility launched by Punjab & Sind Bank in collaboration with NeSL?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**e-Bank Guarantee (e-BG).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Punjab & Sind Bank has launched the e-Bank Guarantee (e-BG) facility in collaboration with National e-Governance Services Ltd (NeSL).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The e-BG facility replaces traditional paper-based Bank Guarantees with e-stamping and e-signatures.**
 
• This new system enhances security, transparency, and efficiency in the Bank Guarantee process.

questions.question: RBI mandates _________ additional run-off factor on digital deposits in April 2025.

Part of Basel III reforms, aiming to ensure banks maintain enough liquid assets to cover 30 days of obligations.

•

• 
 
Align India's regulatory framework with global standards.

 
 
• 
 
Enhance the banking system in a non-disruptive manner.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Digital Banking Services:**

Internet and Mobile Banking (IMB) services include internet banking, mobile banking, and UPI.

 
 
• 
 
These services allow customers to conduct digital transactions from their accounts.

questions.question: In April 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) adjusted its monetary policy stance in response to global economic uncertainties. What was the new stance adopted by the RBI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Accommodative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In April 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) adopted an **Accommodative monetary policy stance** to support economic growth amidst global uncertainties.
 
• An accommodative stance implies that the central bank is ready to lower interest rates or maintain low rates to inject liquidity into the economy.
 
• The decision was taken in response to **slowing global economic growth and subdued inflationary pressures**, ensuring economic stability.
 
• By adopting an accommodative stance, the RBI aimed to encourage borrowing, investment, and spending to boost economic activity in the country.
 
• This policy stance is often employed during periods of **low inflation** and sluggish economic growth to foster recovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy:** It refers to the measures taken by a central bank, like the RBI, to regulate the money supply and interest rates in the economy.
 
• **Accommodative Stance:** This is a policy approach where the central bank lowers interest rates or maintains them at low levels to stimulate economic growth.
 
• **Hawkish vs. Dovish Policy:** A hawkish stance focuses on controlling inflation by increasing interest rates, while a dovish or accommodative stance prioritizes economic growth by lowering rates.
 
• **Global Economic Impact:** Central banks worldwide often adjust their policies in response to global economic trends, such as changes in trade dynamics, geopolitical issues, or financial market volatility.
 
• **Inflation Targeting:** The RBI’s monetary policy framework is guided by inflation targeting, with a medium-term goal of maintaining inflation at 4% (+/- 2%). An accommodative stance is consistent with this framework during periods of low inflation.

questions.question: Which Regional Rural Bank (RRB) was specifically tasked to enhance credit for fisheries and foxnut (makhana) in the Eastern Region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Bihar Gramin Bank.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **The Union Finance Minister recently reviewed the performance of eight Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) from the Eastern Region in a meeting held in Patna.**
 
• **Uttar Bihar Gramin Bank was tasked to enhance credit for fisheries and foxnut (makhana) to realize their regional potential.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The meeting focused on business performance, digital technology upgrades, and fostering growth in agriculture and microindustry-related activities.
 
• RRBs were directed to increase credit disbursement under flagship schemes like MUDRA and PM Vishwakarma.
 
• Technology upgrades have improved efficiency, with the Capital Adequacy Ratio rising from 7.8% in FY 2022 to 9.4% in FY 2024 and GNPA decreasing from 25% to 15%.
 
• RRBs in the Eastern Region recorded a profit of Rs 625 crore in FY 2024 compared to a net loss of Rs 690 crore in FY 2023.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs):**__

 __
 
• Established in 1975 under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976, RRBs provide credit for agriculture and rural sectors.
 
• They combine the cooperative familiarity of rural problems with the professionalism of commercial banks.
 
• The number of RRBs was reduced from 196 in 2005 to 43 in FY21 as part of a consolidation program.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion Initiatives:**__
 __
 
• Schemes like PM Jan Dhan Yojana, PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, and Atal Pension Yojana are being promoted through RRBs.
 
• Sponsor banks are collaborating with RRBs to ensure saturation of beneficiaries under these schemes.
 
 
 
• **Flagship Schemes:**__
 
 
• *Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY):* Launched in 2015 to provide loans up to Rs. 10 lakh for non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• *PM Vishwakarma Yojana:* Aimed at providing financial support to artisans and craftsmen.

questions.question: Which Indian bank is the first to introduce real-time tracking for international transfers through Swift GPI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IDFC FIRST Bank.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **IDFC FIRST Bank has become the first Indian bank to offer real-time tracking for cross-border payments.**

__
 
• **The tracking feature is enabled through Swift GPI (Global Payments Innovation).**
 
• Available on both the bank's Mobile App and Internet Banking platforms.
 
• Provides transparency and convenience for international money transfers.
 
• Allows customers to track payments similarly to UPI or IMPS transactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• Allows banks to track payments in real-time and provides updates to customers.
 
 
 
• UPI__
 
 
• Unified Payments Interface, a real-time payment system developed by NPCI in India.
 
• Allows instant money transfers between bank accounts via mobile devices.
